title: Air India Takes Best Airline and Best Staff Titles at 2026 Skytrax Awards
excerpt: The carrier beat IndiGo to the top of the India & South Asia ranking in the passenger-voted awards, adding a 4-Star certification and Most Improved Airline in Asia to a haul announced in London on September 18.
body:
Air India has been crowned the best airline in India at the 2026 Skytrax World Airline Awards, beating home rival IndiGo to the top spot in a verdict delivered by 24.8 million passengers worldwide. The airline, which announced the honours on September 18, also took home the titles of Best Airline Staff in India & South Asia and a 4-Star Airline Certification for its Business and Economy Class products.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=_MB1stp8eHI

The awards were presented at the Skytrax ceremony held at The Langham hotel in London. Air India’s Chief Executive and Managing Director Campbell Wilson received the honours on behalf of the airline, alongside cabin crew. Beyond the headline categories, Skytrax’s official winners’ list credits the airline with five more India & South Asia titles: Most Improved Airline in Asia, Best Economy Class, Best Economy Class onboard catering, Best Business Class and Best Business Class onboard catering.

Skytrax’s survey is the industry’s heavyweight benchmark. The 2026 edition drew 24.8 million eligible responses from passengers of more than 100 nationalities across 300-plus airlines, polled between September 2025 and August 2026 — a span that covers the airline’s deepening turnaround under the Tata Group.

Context & Background

The win is a marker of how far Air India has travelled since its 2022 privatisation. The airline’s Vihaan.AI programme — a fleet modernisation and cabin-upgrade effort spanning reimagined lounges, digital innovation and employee retraining — has been the engine of its comeback. The Skytrax honours follow its recent elevation from a 3-Star to a 4-Star airline rating, widely treated as a global benchmark for quality.

IndiGo, India’s dominant budget carrier, finished second in the India & South Asia ranking, with Akasa Air third, Air India Express fourth and SriLankan Airlines fifth. IndiGo had its own day: a record 16th win as Best Low-Cost Airline in India & South Asia, plus Best Cabin Crew and Cleanest Airline titles for the region. Globally, the world’s best airline crown went to Singapore Airlines, followed by Qatar Airways and Cathay Pacific.

Not every headline from the Indian market has been celebratory this week — the carrier still contends with the operational scrutiny that follows any legacy airline in transformation — but the passenger-voted nature of these awards is what makes them stick. Unlike editorial judging panels, Skytrax rankings are a direct readout of traveller experience.

Impact & Analysis

The staff award may be the most telling of the set. Air India’s 24,000-plus employees have been the visible front of its transformation, and passenger votes for staff excellence suggest the cultural reset inside the company is registering where it counts — at check-in, in the cabin and on arrival. The Most Improved Airline in Asia title reinforces that the trajectory, not just the current state, impressed voters.

Commercially, the timing is useful. Air India is expanding its nonstop network to North America and Europe, markets where premium travellers compare it directly against Gulf and European flag carriers. A 4-Star certification and best-staff recognition give its sales teams tangible proof points in corporate travel negotiations and premium-cabin marketing.

For IndiGo, second place in the regional ranking is no humiliation given its scale — it flies more than a million passengers every three days — but it underlines a strategic split: IndiGo owns the low-cost crown it has held 16 times, while Air India is capturing the full-service prestige categories.

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora in the United States, this news lands where it is most relevant: the nonstop. Air India operates the largest India–US nonstop network, and for many Indian-American families the choice of carrier for trips home is part habit, part loyalty, part scepticism earned over years of inconsistent service. These awards are the first passenger-voted evidence that the turnaround many have watched with raised eyebrows is being felt in the cabin.

Diaspora travel bookings also skew toward holiday peaks — Diwali, Thanksgiving, Christmas — when reliability and staff handling matter most. Best-staff recognition, earned through a survey covering exactly the international routes these travellers fly, is arguably more persuasive than any advertising campaign.

What’s Next

Wilson framed the awards as momentum, not arrival: the airline says it remains focused on investing in people, products, technology and customer experience. The real test will be the winter schedule — new aircraft deliveries, refreshed cabins on long-haul routes and whether the service consistency that won the votes holds under peak-season load.

Skytrax’s 2027 survey cycle is already underway. For Air India, the target is no longer improvement awards but cracking the global top 20, a tier it has never reached. For now, the airline gets to call itself India’s best — and the passengers said so.

These awards belong to the more than 24,000 Air Indians whose professionalism, warmth, and commitment are driving our transformation every day.

— Campbell Wilson, CEO & Managing Director, Air India
